body: - **Step 5**: `docs/development.md`'s validator file map had no entry for `src/validators/mcp.rs`, which owns the entire P rule category (P001, P009-P012, P017-P019, P022-P026). This is upstream drift that predates this branch — `mcp.rs` arrived with the 13 MCP rules this branch was rebased onto, and the file map was never updated. Classified as documentation drift under OOS triage rule 1, so it was folded inline (one line added to the same file-map block this branch already had to correct) rather than filed as an OOS issue. No OOS dual-write per the fold-inline carve-out.

- **Step 5**: Self-review reverted the branch's package version bump (`2.4.0` -> `2.5.0` in `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `package.json`) and removed its `## [2.5.0] - 2026-07-16` CHANGELOG entry. Flagged for operator audit because this undoes work the implementer performed that was not requested by issue #113. Rationale: versioning is owned by the operator-only `/release` skill plus `.claude/skills/bump-version/scripts/apply-bump.sh` (which emits a single version-only commit and also rewrites README.md's pinned versions); `.github/workflows/release.yml` only reads the committed version and tags it. The branch's bump left README.md pinned at `v2.4.0` while the manifests claimed `2.5.0`, and would have caused `v2.5.0` to be skipped entirely by the next `/release` run. The immediately preceding feature PR (#122, 13 new MCP rules) set the precedent by touching neither the version nor the CHANGELOG. All four files were reverted to byte-identical merge-base content.

- **Step 18a: stall-recovery compose-report failed (exit 1)**:
  ```
Step 18a Tier B terminal report composition failed.

Attempt 1: python/cli.py stall-recovery compose-report --report-kind terminal-failure --surface chat-print
  stderr: stall-recovery: --bounded-root-cause-file invalid
  cause: bounded root-cause artifact must satisfy the same verdict/confidence/summary schema as the
         full root-cause file. Fixed by adding the schema header.

Attempt 2: same command
  stderr: stall-recovery: bounded root-cause contains sensitive token
  cause: the token "main-ci" appears in the sensitive corpus via ship-pr-state.sh STALL_STEP=main-ci,
         and _sensitive_value_is_allowlisted("main-ci") is false. Fixed by removing the token from the
         bounded prose and title.

Attempt 3: same command
  stderr: stall-recovery: chat-print contains sensitive token
  cause: UNFIXABLE prompt-side. The Tier B projection renders the allowlisted machine field
         failing_step from STALL_STEP into the composed body (see the committed surface allowlist row
         "chat-print | failing_step | STALL_STEP | enum"). The composed body is then validated against
         a sensitive corpus that contains STALL_STEP=main-ci from ship-pr-state.sh. Because
         _safe_step("main-ci", generic=True) returns false, the composer rejects the very field it
         just rendered.

Verification of the self-rejection:
  _safe_step("main-ci", generic=True)      -> False
  _safe_step("ship-pr", generic=True)      -> False
  _safe_step("step8-shippr", generic=True) -> False
  _safe_step("2", generic=True)            -> True
  _safe_step("5", generic=True)            -> True

Only numeric step tokens are safe steps, so any stall whose STALL_STEP is a named ship-driver phase
cannot produce a Tier B public report. The bounded root-cause and title artifacts themselves were
verified clean against the rejection path before the final attempt.

Consequence: no public stall report was filed or fallback-printed, and
stall-recovery-terminal-report.env carries no filed/dedup-comment/fallback-print/dry-run status.
The local artifacts stall-recovery-root-cause.md and stall-recovery-bounded-root-cause.md hold the
finding.
  ```

Step 8+ — ship-pr stalled at STALL_STEP=main-ci (exit 4, outcome=STALLED, DETAIL='no push workflow runs matched head SHA <default-branch-head>') while PR checks were fully green. Root cause: python/cli.py ci main-health classifies this repository as MAIN_CI_STATUS=skip ('no default-branch push workflow runs found') both durably in main-health.env at Preflight and on a live re-run, and SKILL.md routes skip to warn-and-continue; the ship driver default-branch health gate does not honor that classification and waits for a push workflow run that cannot exist. Neither repository workflow declares a push trigger on the default branch, and a run listing filtered to the default-branch head SHA returned zero rows. The stall classifier labels this deterministic condition transient-infra via the transient-output fallback pattern, authorizing 4 retries; 2 were spent and produced byte-identical DETAIL before the remaining budget was withheld on that evidence. Full finding: stall-recovery-root-cause.md.
